root_causes: Inefficient exploration behavior by Agent 0: multiple Explore[kitchen_1] actions (steps 0–5) despite already having located the task objects on the counter, leading to unnecessary movement and time.
Underutilization of Agent 1: Agent 1 remains in Wait[None] for most of the episode instead of being used to parallelize object fetching and placement, reducing overall task efficiency.

Redundant high-level rearrange commands: issuing repeated Rearrange[kettle_0, on, stool_18] and Rearrange[potato_1, on, stool_18] (steps 7–11) even after progress is made, causing extra planning cycles and low rewards.

Suboptimal coordination and role allocation: the policy allows Agent 0 to keep holding the kettle and then wait (steps 12–15) instead of finishing placement quickly, while Agent 1 manages the potato, leading to awkward sequencing.

Weak termination/monitoring logic: Wait[None] is chosen at the end (steps 12–16) despite the task being essentially complete, indicating the planner is not tightly synced with the true completion state.
improvement_suggestions: Introduce a progress-aware exploration policy that stops Explore actions once all task-relevant objects (kettle and potato) and a valid target stool are detected, then switches to manipulation immediately.
Implement explicit multi-agent role assignment: e.g., Agent 0 handles the kettle, Agent 1 handles the potato, both plan shortest paths from the counter to nearest stools to maximize parallelism.

Refine the rearrange planner to avoid reissuing identical high-level rearrange commands once an object is already being transported or has been successfully placed, possibly by tracking per-object state (on counter, in hand, placed).
Add a post-condition check to terminate or switch to a no-op policy as soon as all propositions (kettle on any stool, potato on any stool) are satisfied, rather than continuing to issue Wait actions.

Encourage direct pick-and-place sequences: from counter → pick → navigate → place on stool, with minimal intermediate steps; penalize unnecessary wandering or waiting when objects and targets are known.
Enhance coordination logic so that an agent holding an already-placed object (e.g., kettle) is prompted to release it promptly rather than remaining in Wait while holding it.
overall_assessment: The task was ultimately completed successfully, but the trajectory shows significant inefficiencies in exploration, coordination, and termination behavior, leading to unnecessary steps and low reward. Execution quality is functional but far from optimal for a two-agent setting.
task_instruction: Move the kettle and potato from the counter to the stool in the kitchen.
